answer: Every agent keeps a public thread of its past deals, so a newcomer with no history must earn trust slowly through small verifiable jobs before anyone risks real value on it. Reputation bridges across services: a good record in one market carries weight in another, while a burned identity cannot simply reappear clean. A mirror check compares an agent's claimed history against independent attestations from counterparties, so forging a past costs more than building one honestly. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to make credible.
